findings.rationale: An irreversible effect is accepted once an idempotency-key expression is present, but the scaffold metadata passed to code generation omits that expression and carries only request/outcome/retry data. Consequently the generated external-effect boundary cannot implement the declared deduplication key, so retries or concurrent entry can repeat an irreversible payment even though the structural check passes.

Effect ownership is reduced to a global event-name boolean, and the caller suppresses the saga observation action whenever any effect lists that name. No visible validation makes outcome-event ownership exclusive or prevents the same domain event from also being emitted by an aggregate or another effect. Such a shared emission is therefore classified as effect-owned and loses its saga-observation transition, leaving an otherwise valid saga wait unable to advance.
